769.t: Inspirations and first drum set bought in 1919
769.s: He names Henry Martin, Black Benny, Red Happy and Baby Dodds as models, takes press-roll lessons, and buys a first outfit around 1919.
769.q: And, well, he got his inspiration from Bunk. And I got my inspiration from Henry Martin, Black Benny, Red Happy, Baby Dodds. But Baby Dodds used to play in the Orleans during them times. Yeah. Well, after I got old enough I used to go to dances. I, wherever Baby Dodds was playing I was always…

769.t: Opening and growing up in the Third Ward; drum lessons
769.s: Watkins describes the Third Ward jazz neighbourhood, early drummers he admired, and roll lessons from Henry Morton.
769.q: When I started, I started in 1920s. Well that was quite a few years after George Lewis and Paul Barbrain. Well I always did love drums because I was born in the third ward and that was, a section for jazz probably because Lee Armstrong was from that ward. He was born and raised around there. And I…

769.s: Without lessons he learned from watching drummers, practised on a wash tub, and bought a first set of drums while playing house parties with Baby Brewster.
769.q: And I used to watch Baby Dots anytime when I got a chance to go hear them, and I used to watch Henry Martin, I watched Black Benny, and Red Happy, and all those fellas that was making a name for themselves. And, well I never did learn music, I just taken interest, so much interest in it that I fell…

138.t: First drum and flags from the Sugar and Cotton Exposition
138.s: Laine tells how his father bought a field drum and flags at the exposition sale, leading him to organize field, string and brass bands with Dave Perkins's help.
138.q: Yes. Sugar and Cotton Exposition. Well, I had a small little drum, you know, like the Christmas toy drums, you know. Yes. And when the exposition broke up, they were selling out everything there. And, of course, my old man bought me a field drum.

138.t: Learning the drums and first paid job at 14
138.s: Laine's father bought a field drum around the 1885 Cotton Exposition; he led a kids' field band and played his first paid political parade about two years later.
138.q: Oh, I guess. I used to fool at them things when I was just brought up. I think they walked. When the Cotton Exposition came down here, the Sugar and Cotton Exposition, I'm speaking about that, it was way back in 1885. Way back in there. Way back in 1885. My old man happened to buy a drum up there.…

138.t: Laine's first drums, flags and rehearsals on Charter Street
138.s: Laine describes his Christmas-toy drum, field drum and bass drum, the exposition flags, and rehearsing in the basement at Mandeville and Charter.
138.ch: Early drums, photos and the Laine home
138.q: Oh, I muck with music before I started to play. Before I got married, you muck around a kid, you know, before I was married. I was already about 13 years old, so like that, when I started, you know. I had a drum. I believe it was old man Gilmore's boy. I bought it off of him, a Christmas toy, in…

899.t: Starting on drums on the steps
899.s: He began on drums at about 15, beating on the steps, and got his first drums around 19.
899.ch: Learning the drums and first job
899.q: Drums. I used to play on the steps and different things like that until I bought a drum. And then after I bought a snare drum. I, uh...

899.t: First job with trumpeter Euless Jean
899.s: His first job was with Euless Jean, who inspired him to play drums; Jean now lives in Baton Rouge.
899.ch: Learning the drums and first job
899.q: He was a trumpet player, a good friend of mine. Yes, I heard him play one time. Yeah, he's the cause I start playing drums, because he played the trumpet and I said, well, I'll play the drums.

262.t: Teaching himself drums on tubs and pans
262.s: No teacher: he learned on tubs and boxes, nearly lost his delivery job, and his brother bought a pawn-shop drum set.
262.q: I learned on tubs, tin pans, and boxes. Oh yeah, I see. Many people would throw the water at night. I'd be on people's step at 12 o'clock at night with some clean sticks. I was working at Old Magazine Market, trying to have the Old Magazine Market. I liked to have lost my job. I was delivering meat.

262.s: Drums were his first instrument; he also played harmonica, guitar, piano and others, and Allen proposes recording him.
262.q: Drums. That's the first thing I took off, but I played a lot of them used after that.

875.t: First drumming job with Young Morgan and Son Leger
875.s: Howard fills in at a party, is hired by Young Morgan, buys a $62.50 drum set and plays with Son Leger.
875.q: Yeah. I just remember the rest of the fellow, there were about six of us anyway. And I started playing the drum with them and then with Chris, you know, job around with different fellows.

875.t: Wanting to be a trumpeter and learning drums
875.s: Howard says he always wanted trumpet, taught himself drums by watching, and discusses bass drum beating.
875.q: Well, it depends on the tune he was going to play. It's a number. See, now if they're going to play well, if they beat that one beat like that. See? Now, like a lot of drummers right now, I know that's the way you're supposed to play. Yeah, I'm talking about that. But if you get tired, you can ride…

286.t: First instrument drums, lessons, and turning down New York
286.s: He began on drums, took lessons from five or six years old, and says he aimed for the biggest band in the city, passing up New York offers because he earned well at home.
286.q: And see, the average musician there, he goes out for what they got to do. He don't go out for big time. See, when I started, I was going out for the biggest band in the city. Maybe go to New York. Luke Elton, I had the opportunity to go there a couple of times. See, but I was making much money here…

286.t: Foster Lewis band and the friend who built him a drum set
286.s: After two or three years in small bands he joined the Foster Lewis band; a friend made him a set of drums; the band mostly faked rather than read.
286.q: How long did you play with Jim and Jim? Oh, it must have been about two, three years. And after all, the other band, they had a gang of bands around there, a small band. They had no big band around those. No 12, 13-piece bands. The biggest band he had around there was six, seven pieces.

847.t: Taking up drums at about 20, self-taught
847.s: He started on tin cans and boxes, got his first set at about 20, never took lessons, and joined Desvigne's band.
847.q: I used to go around and listen to Buddy Pete Teeth and those guys in the Papa Salstein band. And I always loved to play the drum. I would get on tin cans and tubs, you know, and beat like that.

847.t: His first drum set from a pawn shop
847.s: He bought a Ludwig set with cymbals, wood blocks and tom-toms from a shop on Rampart and played small bars.
847.q: Wood blocks. Had the Chinese cymbals and the gun. I had all that. And I had the tum-toms. Big round tum-toms. I played those. Stayed around. Played those a long time.

55.t: Giving Zutty his drums, Red Allen's start, and Henry Allen's brass band
55.s: Bill gave Zutty Singleton his drum set, helped Red Allen, and played his first street job with Allen's band.
55.ch: Brother Remus and the brass bands
55.q: I used to go follow my brother. Not follow him, but I used to tell him to come at the economy hall and places to help him with his drum like that. I used to carry a drum across the third district ferry. He'd bring the drum backward and forward then. Get up there and I'd play. You know, listen, I…

55.t: Joining Frank Dusen's band and playing snare in brass bands
55.s: Bill sits in with Dusen's band at Algiers, is taken on, and talks about snare versus bass drum with Robichaud and Happy.
55.q: And this old, this old Nancy, Lorenzo Stahl, he was using Lorenzo Stahl on a band. I remember that good. See, now that was a, that's what all he used to use around here. People call us a Dixon Lane. That been going on. Sure. For years, that been going. We were raised like that. We just didn't use…

766.t: Taking up drums with no lessons
766.s: He started drums at about 19 on a regular set and never took lessons.
766.q: Well, I already played drum. I always was a drummer, I mean.

766.t: Teaching himself and buying drums at Coins
766.s: He picked drums on his own, with no inspiring drummer, and bought a set from Coins Music Company.
766.q: Well, I just took it up on my own. I mean, I haven't watched anybody really. I just took it up on my own.

832.s: He took no drum lessons, only sax lessons. He bought drums through a man named Peterson with a music store, then went with different bands in New Orleans.
832.q: I take a bunch of drums here and went over to the same boy, Harold Peterson. The first man they showed me, they had the whole drum stick.

832.t: Coming to New Orleans in 1922 and getting drums
832.s: Foster confirms he crossed the lake in 1922, with drums bought in 1921, and played first with Amos Riley.
832.q: Yeah. That's where he was here. That's where he had left him over there. Yes, yes. Well he came over, he came from, how do I think, Charlie, Charlie.

302.t: Drumming on the steps and first drum set
302.s: He began beating on box steps with chair rounds at six or seven and bought his first drum set at about fourteen.
302.q: First I bought the snare, then I bought the stand and the bass drum, you know what I mean? So it touched like that.

302.t: Playing along with records at family fish fries
302.s: He learned by playing along with Celestin and Oliver records, and played at his mother's Saturday fish fries.
302.q: Well, I'll tell you. We had one of those old graphophones, you know, the graphophones with a big horn, you know. My daddy used to buy the records of Celestine and King Oliver and those fellas, you know.

825.s: Ernie picked up drums without lessons. His brother, the oldest in the family, was about eighteen years older and played in short pants with Bunk Johnson.
825.q: Oh, he's the oldest one in the family. Right now he would be about 63. No, he would be about 68 right now.

825.t: Why he gave up drums: carrying a set in the 1920s
825.s: Ernie loved drums but hauled a set by streetcar with a city-hall permit, and rides were hard to get. As a boy he went to jobs his brother passed to him.
825.ch: Drumming days and neighborhood life, 1919 onward
825.q: still play drums because you have to i'll tell you matter of fact drums was the instrument that i liked i really like drums and up to right now some of these drummers i hear if i had me a set up here i think i would take them but i is at the time i was playing drums this was the handicap in the…

311.t: Getting his first drumset from Jess Priserssen and being helped by others
311.s: A Swedish drum-shop owner gave him bargains, and he says help from people of all races kept him free of prejudice.
311.q: Oh yeah. I got my first set from a guy names Jess Priserssen, I think he was from Sweden. Anyway he had a drum shop downtown here and he took a liking to me. That’s my luck. People just took a liking to me and helped me a lot. I got a lot of help from other people and that’s why I was never…

311.t: Growing up in San Francisco, job discrimination, winning the grammar school drum contest
311.s: Alley says hiring was racially closed (no streetcar or bus jobs) so he red capped and shined shoes; he became a drummer by winning a grammar school contest for free lessons.
311.q: All together different. I can tell you some reasons why. One reason, when I first grew up in Francisco there were two unions, there wasn’t one union, and when I got out — the reason I became a musician, when I got out of school, why it was hard to get a job at different places, in those days,…

493.t: Toy drums, piano lessons and the violin
493.s: His first music was a toy drum set at three, a few piano lessons and violin through a Montessori school deal. He sat in on drums at his father's show at six.
493.q: The first story that I was told, as far as music was concerned, had to do when I was three. The story involved this little toy drum set. There’s a picture of that too. There’s a picture of me behind this toy drum set. The story was that they would play a game and introduce me playing these drums.…

493.t: First sit-in at Snug Harbor and the pull of the orchestra's percussion section
493.s: He recalls his first sit-in with his father at Snug Harbor and fewer chances to play in Richmond. Seeing the percussion section in the youth orchestra ended his violin days.
493.ch: First drum teachers and early training
493.q: At this point I was playing drums and violin off and on, but it wasn’t as consistent, because in Richmond there weren’t as many chances to play as there were in New Orleans. In New Orleans, my father was working every week at Snug Harbor, which he still does. We’re still there, after all these…

377.s: Basie says there were no kid's bands in his youth, that he played a little drums first, and that drums were his first love; the full story is saved for his book.
377.ch: Early career: vaudeville and Kansas City
377.q: They didn't have (Inaudible) no kid's band in them years. (Laughter.) There were no bands in them kind of years. There were no bands. Didn't have no kid bands. (Inaudible) nowhere. (Laughter.)

377.t: Giving up drums and the person who 'ran him to the piano'
377.s: Basie says he taught himself on a bass drum and a small drum, and teases that someone who will walk into the room 'run him to the piano'; a chain pendant is mentioned.
377.ch: Early career: vaudeville and Kansas City
377.q: I was very young, very young (inaudible). Of course, I wasn't too young for girls, of course, you know. But then I was, in a way, because (inaudible) people thought a little differently about (inaudible) certain age, or something like that, to be chasing.

381.t: Resuming on August 16: wanting a drum from age four
381.s: Francis restarts his story: cardboard Christmas drums that lasted a week, and the family's UNIA membership.
381.ch: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
381.q: four, that it was Christmas time and my mother and father asked me what I wanted for Christmas, and I told them I wanted a drum.

381.t: Lettego, cousin Harold and the first drummer who inspired him
381.s: He recalls a Bahamian drummer nicknamed Lettego, with a megaphone on the snare, at his father's bootleg parties, and his father's opposition to music.
381.ch: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
381.q: Well, there was a guy in Miami, his last name was Abrista, but one night a couple of guys got in a fight, and he was from the Bahamas and he was telling the guys to let him go, but instead of saying let him go, he said, "lette go", and he got this nickname, "Lettego", and everybody used to call him…

147.t: High school playing with no practice, and the first big bass drum
147.s: He did not practice, played stock arrangements, and describes his first huge bass drum, later made into a coffee table.
147.ch: Learning the drums and early influences
147.q: Didn't know what to practice, just get on the jobs and play what came to my mind. Of course, I had to coincide. I had to fit in with what they were playing. No, I didn't practice.

147.t: Stealing from other drummers and the first beats he played
147.s: Crawford says he learned by watching, played four on the bass drum with press rolls, and loves his drums.
147.ch: Learning the drums and early influences
147.q: I didn't have no musical knowledge of drumming or just on what I could see from other drummers and pick up. Oh, yes, I was a stealer.

455.t: Switching to drums; Dallas drummers and Alphonso Trent's band
455.s: Keg gets a trombone, Budd gets drums, admires Texas drummers and Alphonso Trent's sharp band, and becomes one of the best local drummers.
455.q: Keg, Keg Johnson, yes. So I told my mother, I said, "I want to play drums," because there was a couple of drummers around, you know, like I had seen A. Godley G. Gottlieb with Alphonso Trent's orchestra, and then that was a very good drummer that went to school. He was my brother's age, maybe a…

455.t: Snare drum at school and the first boyhood band
455.s: He drums for the marching lunch lines at school and forms a band with Keg and neighborhood friends.
455.q: So I started taking my drum -- the snare drum -- buckle it on to me, to school when I was in elementary school. I think maybe by then I was in about the third grade. And I never will forget my teacher. She was a beautiful lady named Mrs. Bailey, and I used to play --

175.t: Playing kazoo clarinet and bass drum
175.s: In the boys' band he played a clarinet-shaped kazoo and alternated with bass drum, inspired by a loud drummer and Manuel Perez's band.
175.q: No, there was no real clarinet but it was a kazoo made in the shape of a clarinet. Oh I see. And then too I used to alternate from the clarinet to the bass drum, because I used to like to beat the bass drums. And one particular fella around there at that time, I used to call him, I don't remember…

177.t: Moving to New Orleans and buying his first drums
177.s: He moved to New Orleans at about 16, lived with his grandmother and Uncle Oscar, and bought a $25 secondhand set from a pawnshop with wages from a $9-a-week job.
177.q: Well when I came down from Thibodeau to New Orleans, I moved with my grandmother. And she lived with her son Oscar Giles. And I told him I thought I had interest that I would like to play a drum. So I worked at the Crescent Steen Partridge Way. I was getting nine dollars a week. I decided I wanted…

402.t: Starting on drums: Jazzy Leo, a cheese box, first jobs and lessons
402.s: Sal got his first lessons on drums from a delivery-truck driver, made a drum from a cheese box, played house parties and the Slipper, learned to read, and later played in the WPA band.
402.ch: Learning drums, WPA band and dance halls
402.q: It's a funny thing, Dick. I got started playing drums. I'm doing vacation. I got a little job in the field, you see. Delivery boy, bundle boy. And Leo was my driver, but I didn't know he played drums, man. So, I used to call him Jazzy Leo all the time. I wonder why they call him that. When he come…

243.t: Why he started on drums, and early heroes Bucket and Ransom
243.s: Breaux says he took up drums just to get into the band, and recalls sneaking in to watch Bucket play drums and liking Ransom's bass.
243.q: No, I don't know how I got tangled up with the drum. At that time, I don't think I was any more than about 11 or 12 years old. And, uh, I just wanted to get in the band. I didn't care what I played. You know, I imagine that's the way I must have felt. You didn't hang around the big 25 or

246.t: Not travelling to hear bands; Dr. Tudry raised him and he began playing at 21
246.s: Glass says he didn't go to other sections as a boy, was raised by Dr. Tudry at Elysian Fields and Claiborne, and started playing at 21.
246.q: No. That's when they'd come and get me to play, you see. Because Dr. Tudray had raised me, you see, and I just got out. Like that, Lysian Field and Claiborne, that's who adopted me, Dr. Tudray. Well I started playing when I was 21 years old. And I got out. I went to play music. And I just took a…

999.t: First job, then joining Kid Howard's orchestra; self-taught
999.s: His first job was a trio with Harrison Verrett and Homer Eugene, using borrowed drum parts; Kid Howard then took him into his ten-piece band. He never learned to read music.
999.q: Well, he had a tambourine. He used to have one hooked on the side of it. He was driving. He had this side cymbal and a little ball on it. Connected to his ball that hit the bass drum and this little thing would hit that cymbal. Well, that answer for us like they got sock cymbals today. Mm-hmm. That…

249.t: Starting on drums around 1914 and Army band
249.s: He began on drums about 1914, working for a boss, and later went into the Army band.
249.q: No. Well, I was a good age. I was working, you know. Yeah. And played for the work with Slack. Mm-hmm. Probably in Bonnet Petit took me first. Oh, yeah. Yeah, yeah. Well, I got more money I was making that. And the boss sent for me, so I quit. So I kept on playing. I went to the Army. I was known…

871.t: First job at Tom Anderson's with the Duconge brothers; drum sound
871.s: Bigard started on drums, had lessons with Cantrell, and had his first job at Tom Anderson's cabaret with the Duconge brothers; he talks about his Ludwig drums and old-time melodic drumming.
871.q: With Sidney Desvines Orchestra. Can you tell us how you started in music? Your first instrument, what it was? Did you start on drums or something else? On drums. On drums. On drums. I've taken lessons with Professor Cantrell. Oh, yes. Old man, Lloyd Cantrell, was playing drums with Peter Ones…

474.t: Taking up drums before his stroke
474.s: Jones learned drums by watching drummers, played one job, then suffered a stroke.
474.ch: Kid Rena, the Cadillac and Jones's sons
474.q: Played one job then I got the stroke. I got my sticks and everything. I got the avenue in my thing. I got everything. I was ready.

183.t: Giving up the drums because he had to be carried around
183.s: After about five years on drums, Watts tells his father he is tired of the drums and the carrying, and wants to stop.
183.q: Well, I'd say about, I'd say about five years. I never worked with anyone else but him as a drummer. See? And then, shortly after that, my dad, they came back home to visit us. And whenever they come home off the road, they usually stay about two months. See? That's the only time our family saw our…

634.t: Beating on porch steps with chair rounds
634.s: His first instrument was drums, played with chair rounds on neighbours' steps until they ran him off with buckets of water.
634.q: With chair rounds. And the people used to run me off, off they step and I would go on somebody else's step and tell them they run me off.

184.t: Brother Tubby gives him his first sticks
184.s: Tubby, called Baby, handed him a pair of sticks and he began beating on porch steps; this is how he picked up drumming.
184.q: Yeah, that was his nickname, Baby. I thought he was the youngest in the family. No, no, they called him Baby. And one day I was fooling around on St. Yolens, we used to call them Steps, Front Steps, and Gary and all that stuff. So he gave me a pair of sticks one day. So I started to beat around on…

257.t: Polio, instruments in the house, first drums at school
257.s: Braced from polio, he was given instruments at home; drums came first, taught by Sister Cyril, and he played in the school band.
257.q: Yeah, over the thirties, yeah. But matter of fact, I had just started playing trombone professionally then. Yeah. Because see, I've been learning music ever since I was, well I say born, you see. Yeah. Because I had polio, and I was full of braces, so he bought all the instruments and put it at the…

258.t: Uncle Adolph's guitar, first drum set and first job
258.s: He got interested listening to his uncle, bought a junior drum set at 13 and played his first job with the Nelsons at a park for two dollars.
258.q: That's how I become interested in it. I used to sit down and listen to my uncle Adolf play the guitar. He had one particular song he used to play all the time. It was, Baby Just a Spoonful. Yeah, I don't know that. And I was a kid and I'd just, he'd sit on the porch and play that when he'd get down…

706.t: The five-year-old boy backstage in Oregon
706.s: Armstrong tells of a small child who came to his dressing room and played the beat naturally.
706.q: Well, uh, I've worked several times as a kid during my travels, you know what I mean? Then, uh, I'll turn the emphasis of a little kid about five years old, coming to my dressing room when I was playing for it in Oregon at the Paramount Theater, and his mom and father bought him up. Then, uh, they…

45.t: Learning drums: pots and pans, renting a drum, no lessons
45.s: Williams began on his mother's pots at about eight, rented a drum from Dave Puykins, never took lessons and played left-handed.
45.q: Oh, the pick-up drums to learn it? Well, I must have been about eight. Eight. About eight years old. I used to play on the front steps, take my mother's dishpan and pots and play on those. Yeah. On her safe, old safe then, what they call a cabinet, kitchen cabinet, not old safe. I used to play on…

628.t: Born 1906 and taking up the drums
628.s: Williams was born in New Orleans in 1906 and loved drums, following parades and bass drummers like Black Benny. His mother bought him a snare drum, and he went on to play with Joseph Thomas before forming a group with Lawrence Marrero and George Lewis.
628.ch: Beginnings and early New Orleans scene
628.q: Yeah, you want to start now. Born here in New Orleans, 1906 September 22nd. Raised in New Orleans. Raised in New Orleans. What's that? Right here. Down Philly Shandris Street. Which? Philly Shandris. Down the night war. That's what I was born at. Did you hear much music around the house, your…

794.t: Barry Martin's start and his trip to New Orleans
794.s: Background of drummer Barry Martin from Virginia Water, his early bands, Studio 51 residency, and his 1961 journey to New Orleans where he made two recordings.
794.ch: Barry Martin and New Orleans tours to England
794.q: Barry Martin spring? He's a sort of hometown boy from a place called Virginia Water. His father's family comes from a musical family. His mother sang at one time. His father, I believe, played saxophone, or he played drums or saxophone in his small dance bands for many years, and he went into the…

281.t: Origin of the nickname Muggsy and first drums
281.s: He was torn between baseball, music and medicine and was nicknamed after John McGraw; he began as a school drummer leading a Christmas morning band.
281.q: Well, I've, I was torn between three loves. Baseball, music, and medicine. And, uh, I was gonna make a training trip with the Giants when I was 14 years old. Yeah. And, uh, I was nicknamed Muggsy on account of Muggsy McGraw, then the manager of the New York Giants, because he was a spicy little…

819.t: Learning drums, early playing and the Giardina rags
819.s: Sbarbaro was self-taught on drums, started in 1912, played with Giardina in 1914-15 and left in 1916.
819.q: I got a real good set to start out with. I got a set that cost me those days $100, which was a lot of money for just two drums.

570.t: Starting on drums with a tub and cheese-box snare
570.s: Began drums at twelve on a tub and a cheese keg with homemade sticks; Jake Johnson tried to teach him, no formal lessons.
570.q: Well, we had some drumsticks was made for me to use. Mr. Jake Johnson made a pair of sticks for me. And I had one of those round kegs that cheese used to come in. For snare drum. That was my first set I started on.

49.t: Starting on drums, his mother's objections and the hocked snare drum
49.s: Hazel tells how his father bought his snare drum, later pawned it, and how he found it again at a marching club and began professional playing at about 14.
49.q: Well, I played the, after Hardy, after, after we moved on this side of the river. My dad was, used to drink quite a bit. See, mother didn't want me to play music at all.

924.t: Playing drums in Sam Clark's band in Versailles
924.s: Jones recalls drumming as a young man in Sam Clark's band at home, naming members, and buying a drum set, and when he retired and returned.
924.q: I was at home then, I was in my team. I was a young boy, playing drums. He had all four of them learned how to play drums.

1041.t: First violin and drum lessons; tin pans and first drum set
1041.s: He began on violin with Professor Taylor, took drum lessons from Dave Poikins, played on tin pans, and bought his first drum set on a dollar a week.
1041.q: My first instrument when I started playing was violin. I was taking violin lessons from a professor by the name of Professor Taylor. I was taking lessons from him for a while. I started taking lessons from Professor Poikins.

192.t: Brother Sam's drums as his model
192.s: He followed his brother Sam's style and used Sam's drums until he bought his own.
192.q: My brother was a drummer way before my time, you know, and I come right behind him. That was way back in 1919 and 1920. He played with different bands around here like Lewis, you know, and Kid René and all of them. And I just took the style behind him, pick it up behind him. He gave it up in the…

688.t: His brother's drum set and changing his own drums
688.s: Discussion of the drums he learned on; his brother kept the same set while he changed drums often.
688.q: Because he... I changed drums plenty, but he didn't.

290.t: Henry Ford, violinist, and playing drums before trumpet
290.s: He knew two Henry Fords, played drums for about two years with the younger violinist, then switched to trumpet.
290.q: Yeah, I knew them. Henry Ford, tell you the truth, if you're talking about the elder days, two Henry Fords, a young one and an older one. And the young one, he was a violinist. And I played drums with him for quite a while, you know, he had three or four, he didn't have a big orchestra, three or…

295.t: First drum set, first band in the Spanish-American War, and early teachers
295.s: He got his first set at 12-14, led a 35-piece band in the Spanish-American War, and learned from Dave Perkins and Will Meade; his father was not a musician.
295.q: Well, I was doing... when I had my own band, I was doing the Spanish and American War. I had then, in the Spanish and American War, I had 35 pieces, including myself. And after that, well before that rather, I used to play music right on, play field band music in different kinds of instruments with…

25.t: First drums, tin-can bands and school band
25.s: He drummed on buckets and fences, played in tin can bands, then learned in an industrial school band and played dances with a piano player.
25.q: Oh, I had sticks, homemade sticks made from chairs, wooden chairs, and I could always somehow beat rhythm with those sticks.

308.t: Family drummers, birth and first drum set
308.s: His brother Sam played drums; he was born 1904, taught himself, bought a snare around 1921 and a Conn set in the mid-1920s.
308.q: The 23rd February? Yeah. Uh so who taught you to play? Well I didn't exactly I just got some pointers from old man Contra. I just picked up. I just picked up drums myself around the house like that. You know. Yeah. I was listening to old time uh Grafenolis in the piano. It was called me and the…

910.t: Starting on drums after an Italian parade
910.s: In fifth grade he followed a parade, got a whipping, and asked to play drums. He learned from Paul Weckesser, played weddings and dances, and studied with Bill West in New York.
910.q: I started out on drums, I was in the fifth grade. And we had an account at a little Italian store around the corner and my mother sent me to the store to get a loaf of bread and a bottle of milk. And an Italian parade came by. And I came back about four hours later with the milk and the bread, and…

437.t: Getting sticks, a snare and the jelly bean drumset
437.s: He gets his first sticks and snare, sits in on his father's job, and is rewarded with drums for finishing books.
437.q: Well my father didn’t want me in the business, so like I said I had gotten a pair of drum sticks from a drummer, and then I got a snare drum from another drummer, oh wow. I was on my way. And eventually my father got into a pickle once and needed a drummer. His drummer didn’t show up. So he made…

421.t: Starting on drums in Plainfield and lessons with Professor Churchillo
421.s: As a child he was fascinated by the vaudeville pit drummer; his father traded bread for drum lessons from Professor Churchillo, who insisted on solfeggio first; he then played in the professor's band.
421.q: I started as a drummer. I was fascinated with drums as a child, you know, in the vaudeville theaters, see the pit drummer that was standing watching everything that was going on, you know he’d hit a ratchet and blow a whistle with a dum-bang, and catch all the kicks and everything, and I said wow,…

341.t: Getting her first drums and joining the jazz band
341.s: After Buddy Rich she pleaded for drums; her mother bought the wrong drum, and a teacher pushed her to try out for the high school jazz band.
341.ch: Growing up in Endicott and learning drums
341.q: I actually pleaded with my mother to buy me a drum set which was like there is just no way, you know, my daughter is not playing the drums kind of attitude. But then after my pleading and screaming I remember she bought me a, I begged for a snare drum, which is the first drum you would get, and she…

759.t: First drum, the basement drum set and daily practice
759.s: He got his first drum at nine, then a drum set, and practiced six to eight hours a day in the basement at home.
759.q: Well kind of. Not so much the pots and pans. I did bang on everything else around the house, and when I was nine years old I talked my mother into buying my first drum. It was an old medium Ludwig parade drum. For those of you who are going to be watching this overseas, it was medium Ludwig. I used…

222.t: Drum lessons with Johnny Otis and junior high drumming
222.s: He took up drums, studied with Johnny Otis, and played in school bands but found carrying drums a chore.
222.ch: Growing up in the Bay Area
222.q: Well I don’t know. I ran into a road block in junior high school I decided I wanted to be a drummer. And I’d already been playing classical music and a little jazz. And for some reason — oh my cousin was a drummer, and he loaned me some of his drums and my parents weren’t too happy about that idea…

224.t: Building his first drum set from a Boston trio job
224.s: He bought a cymbal or tom-tom each week while playing nights in the Italian section of Boston.
224.q: First drum. Good idea. I never had a complete set when I started. I had bits. When I was still in high school, I was working, I think, five nights a week in the Italian section of Boston. We had to play shows there for tap dancers and play for singers. It was just a little trio. Each week I would…

471.t: The pawnshop saxophone, Jack Denay and Washington drummers
471.s: He bought a C-melody saxophone, lost it, then studied snare drum with percussionist Jack Denay and names drummers Fats Clark, Maurice Lowes and Mack Simpkins.
471.ch: Growing up and learning drums in Washington
471.q: But there was no major anybody said, “You’re going to play some music here, boy,” except for maybe Walter, just hanging out there. Walter – I had – once with him, I was passing a pawn shop somewhere, and I looked and saw a saxophone in the window. I think it must have been somewhere like 17th and U…

111.t: Buying his first drum set and practicing with Hank
111.s: He returned to his mother's house, paid cash for a Ludwig set bought in Detroit, and Hank taught him to play along with Art Tatum records.
111.q: No, I stayed at home. We had a great bit house up there. Thad was gone, Hank was gone, and my sister was married. There wasn’t nobody there except for my mother. It wasn’t like the whole family was—it wasn’t crowded or anything like that. I could practice and I made a lot of noise. But I knew what…

4.t: Origin of the piano-and-drums act and the San Francisco earthquake
4.s: Johnny was a saloon pianist; after the 1906 earthquake, where Reb led him to his operation, he got the idea of adding drums, which made them a sensation in Arizona.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: Well, he was just a piano player then, see? He didn't have a musical act. We formed the act. See, when he took me with him, then we built into the act, but before that, he was a

146.t: Blue Devils get stranded in Dallas and recruit Smith
146.s: The Blue Devils, his first big band, got stranded in Dallas and drummer Ernest Williams came to Smith's house to hire him; he played clarinet and alto though he could not read.
146.q: No. Never did. When I joined up the big band... The biggest band I joined in them days, the first big band in fact, was the Blue Devils. And they came...

758.t: Drum lessons with Mr. Catlett and Joe's objection
758.s: He studied band drumming with Mr. Catlett (not related to Sid), but Joe said drums were too bulky to carry.
758.q: : Then I took drum lessons for a while with Mr. Catlett. He was the best drummer around there as far as band drumming was concerned, you know.

72.s: He whittled broken chair rungs into drumsticks, with no idea about rolls.
72.q: good and Mother had 'em throwed out in the back yard. I'd go out there and get them, and take a cake knife, a knife and a fork...the knife, not the fork...

385.t: Born in Newport News; school band drums and the flood
385.s: Grimes gives his birth as about 1916, says only his mother sang in church, and recalls playing drums in a high school band until a flood ended the dancehall job.
385.q: Well really the question should be why was I born. I was born in Newport News, Virginia I think, approximately 7-7-16. I was always musically inclined, no one in my family was -- except my mother sang in church -- While I was in school they had a little band there, and I took up drums. Well, I was…

386.t: Professor Cobb's cornet lessons and early lodge drummers
386.s: At seven he takes two weeks of lessons from Professor Cobb, who tells his mother he has no musical aptitude; he then notices lodge bands and drummers.
386.q: Well, what happened was, when I was about seven, there was a man that played a cornet, named Professor Cobb, a rarity. And I asked my mother if I could take lessons with Professor Cobb, and she said yes. And Professor Cobb taught me for two weeks, 25 cents a lesson. And then he talked to my mother…

387.t: Playing drums and trying every instrument
387.s: He played drums and trumpet together and rented other instruments out of curiosity.
387.q: Yes, with a trumpet band; I played the trumpet and the drums. I used to take dates like that. I had a record player, it even had a straw needle on it and I played the drums with whoever was around on the record or the radio. I played the trumpet at the same time. That all went together.

427.t: Wanting to be a drummer, beating on his mother's pans
427.s: Watching drummers through club windows, he beat on pots and pans with chair sticks and declared he'd be a drummer.
427.q: And then we had a lot of toys that he had, so when... I always wanted to play the drums. I don't know where I got that from but I

149.t: Starting on drums and tin cans
149.s: He began beating tin cans and a picket fence, then carried a snare drum in the school band at about six.
149.q: Well, I started just like I said. I'd take two sticks and beat on tin cans. And then, of course, we had a picket fence and I used to play that. And then, when I got to the age of maybe 6, I'm not sure, 6, just large enough to carry a snare drum, then they put me in the band. Then I just crew from…

115.t: Practising at home; his mother buys him a snare drum
115.s: He had been practising at home on a small drum his mother had bought; seeing he was serious she then bought a snare drum.
115.ch: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
115.q: Well, she bought that little drum for me, I would say, about ten or 11 years old.

237.t: Learning drums from his brother Bud on a lard bucket
237.s: Smith recaps Lovett's life since 1894 and asks how he began; he copied his brother James 'Bud' Lovett on a lard bucket and cans.
237.ch: Learning drums and recording on the Coast
237.q: That's right. He taught me how to play. Well, I -- he didn't teach me but I could hear him practicing at home there, you know, and he has fine drums, had his fine drums set up. Man, I'd get me a lard bucket and go out and --

76.t: Aunt Carrie, first drums and the second line bands
76.s: His Aunt Carrie, a teacher and pianist, and his mother encouraged him; she bought his first drums. He beat on chairs, followed New Orleans second-line bands and moved there at about ten.
76.q: Yes, she's the one that partly raised me in a way because she was an old school teacher and I used to go to Bunkie and (Upper Lousay?) and Mamou (Marmout?), that's in Louisiana.

238.s: Talmadge started on piano, then drums with Lenny Rosenthal, but lost interest when his teacher changed.
238.q: don't -- you know, I don't say that I would have wanted him to be a professional musician, you know. That would be up to him to choose this, and I think this is the way it should be with any child. I don't think you should just force it on him. But I was hoping that he would have been musical, you…

171.t: First instruments: timber blocks, Boy Scout drums, ukulele
171.s: He tried timber blocks, field drums in the Boy Scouts, a school quartet and the ukulele, and mentions Sergeant Willis.
171.ch: Growing up with music in Austin
171.q: No, actually I had -- I borrowed some things called temple blocks. Now, this would be -- well what Lionel Hampton used them, but it was made out of wood. Did you ever see those? Usually drummers would use those.

103.t: First snare drum and people he met around Birmingham
103.s: Jones describes the snare drum his aunt bought and his Birmingham, Alabama neighborhood, naming people who shaped his life.
103.q: Well, with a series of things but I remember that my aunt bought me this snare drum and I was trying to do other things and everybody in the neighborhood, the kids, in the various one of the last neighborhoods I stayed in, they had come out to play just the snare drum. And throughout that later on…

98.t: Starting on drums in the Milwaukee school band
98.s: The school started a band; he took drum lessons from a Milwaukee Symphony drummer for ten cents each and says he was always a drummer, beating on pots and fences.
98.ch: Childhood, first drums and the hustling years
98.q: In Milwaukee, there. See, at the school, they wanted to start a band. So they just picked out the different kids and asked each one of them what instrument they wanted to play. And then they had an association with the Milwaukee Symphony. And so I took drums from this Symphony drummer in Milwaukee,…
